answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The opal multiplier is published, charged in shale, and dune lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3660 identities would post 2878 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
